clue.text: Having more knowledge despite having wires crossed

indicators.note: wires that are crossed are tangled up, so the letters of the word are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone ends up better informed even though the conversation went badly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having wires crossed' sounds like a misunderstanding; 'crossed' is the anagram signal for WIRES.
explanation.definitionFit: To be wiser is to have greater learning or understanding than before.

clue.text: Observe some letters making up the phrase

parts.note: to observe is to watch
a word is a group of letters

explanation.surface: Someone is told to watch the letters that form a saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A watchword is a slogan or motto, a phrase that sums up a principle.

clue.text: Cut small amount of grain in the outhouse

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: a shed is an outhouse
an ear of corn is a seed-bearing head of grain

explanation.surface: A farmer trims some corn kept in an outbuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheared means cut or clipped, as wool from sheep.

clue.text: Space to tie up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to moor a boat is to tie it up

explanation.surface: Someone needs enough space to fasten a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Room means space or capacity, as in room to move.

clue.text: Suffer an ordeal in the Big Top perhaps

definitions.text: Suffer an ordeal in the Big Top perhaps

parts.words: Suffer an ordeal in the Big Top perhaps
parts.note: the idiom for enduring a testing experience is pictured literally as a circus performer leaping through a ring under the tent

explanation.surface: A circus act endures a gruelling time under canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: The Big Top is the circus tent, where animals and acrobats literally leap through rings; the idiom means to undergo a trying experience.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means enduring a testing or humiliating process, as circus animals are made to jump through rings.

clue.text: Going ahead with illegal roof stripping?

definitions.meaning: a literal reading: stealing the metal sheeting from a roof

explanation.surface: Thieves are pressing on with stripping metal from a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means moving into first place, and literally describes thieves stealing roofing metal.

clue.text: English girl loses her head for Frenchman

indicators.note: losing a head means the opening letter of the name is taken away

parts.note: Irene is a girl's name common in England

explanation.surface: An English woman is beheaded for love of a Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: René is a common French masculine given name.

clue.text: It is vain to economise

explanation.surface: A remark that trying to save money is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: to economise is to USE LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Useless means futile or having no purpose, the sense of in vain.

clue.text: Dislikes inordinate haste

indicators.note: inordinate means excessive or disordered, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone can't stand excessive hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Hates means detests or strongly dislikes.

clue.text: See 4
Spectacular results here when strings are pulled

definitions.text: Spectacular results here when strings are pulled

parts.words: Spectacular results here when strings are pulled
parts.note: pulling strings sounds like using influence, but here it is literal: wires moving figures in a show

explanation.surface: A remark on how influence-peddling gets impressive results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strings are pulled' suggests string-pulling influence; in fact marionettes are worked on strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A puppet theatre stages shows with marionettes worked by strings.

clue.text: Most courteous about the stink 'e'd produced

indicators.note: produced suggests making something new from material, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the dropped-aitch form of he'd, giving ED

explanation.surface: A cockney speaker complains about the smell someone made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'E'd is 'he'd' with the H dropped; its letters ED join STINK to be rearranged, signalled by 'produced'. 'About' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindest is the superlative of kind, meaning the most considerate and gracious.

clue.text: Damage caused by enemy leader leaving women's quarters

indicators.note: leaving means the named letter departs from the word, so it is removed

parts.note: a harem is the women's quarters in a Muslim household

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A raid by the opposing chief on the women's quarters causes destruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To harm is to injure or damage; as a noun it means injury.

clue.text: Backbone of the turnkey?

parts.note: a turnkey is a jailer, but read as turn plus key it gives a word for turn followed by E, a musical key

explanation.surface: Asks about the spinal column of a prison warder.
explanation.walkthrough: A turnkey is a jailer; split it as 'turn' (SPIN) plus 'key' (E, a musical key) and you have the vertebral column.
explanation.definitionFit: The spine is the backbone, the column of vertebrae down the back.

clue.text: Not as much in Charles' savings

indicators.note: in tells the solver the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A man named Charles has fewer savings than expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Less means a smaller amount, the comparative of little.

clue.text: Said in France to mean a repeat order

parts.note: dit is French for said
taken as written

explanation.surface: A French speaker explains a word for ordering the same again.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto is the word or mark meaning the same again, as in repeating an order.

clue.text: Unaspirated greeting coming from the Stirling area

indicators.note: said without the breathy aitch sound, so that letter is removed

parts.note: halloa is an old call of greeting or to attract attention

explanation.surface: A Scot from near Stirling says hello without an H.
explanation.walkthrough: Alloa is a town on the Forth near Stirling, in central Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Alloa is a small Scottish town lying just east of the city of Stirling.

clue.text: Superstitious widows' stories?

parts.note: widows were once married women, so their tales are those of former spouses, a playful reading of the phrase for folk superstitions

explanation.surface: Asks whether widows tell credulous stories.
explanation.walkthrough: Widows are, literally, women who were once wives, which gives a jokey reading of the stock phrase for unfounded folk beliefs.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes traditional but unfounded beliefs passed down by word of mouth.

clue.text: New rate more certain to be official

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: surer means more certain

explanation.surface: A fresh rate is more reliable, says the officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer is the officer responsible for an organisation's funds.

clue.text: Has a smashing time, starts to drink too much

definitions.meaning: literally strikes the glass container, as in breaking a bottle
the idiom for taking to heavy drinking

explanation.surface: A party-goer enjoys themselves and begins to overindulge in alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means taking to heavy drinking, and literally means striking a glass container.

clue.text: I rather upset the girl

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, signalling the letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone admits annoying a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Harriet is a female given name.

clue.text: It is hard work keeping a number in low

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to trail is to be behind, lagging low in a contest
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Toiling while a figure stays depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAIL keeps A and V (five in Roman numerals) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is painful or laborious effort.

clue.text: Banking system used by Inland Revenue in turn

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: a turn in a game is a go
IR is the abbreviation for the Inland Revenue, the former UK tax authority

explanation.surface: The tax office uses a particular way of transferring money.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inland Revenue was the British tax office before 2005.
explanation.definitionFit: Giro is a system of direct money transfer between bank or post-office accounts.

clue.text: Confined to college despite having entrance key

parts.note: a gate is an entrance
D is a musical key

explanation.surface: A student is kept in despite holding a key to the gate.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge, a student who is gated is forbidden to leave college.
explanation.definitionFit: Gated is the British university term for a student confined to college as a punishment.

clue.text: A number of trees in Kent

parts.note: seven is a number
oaks are trees

explanation.surface: A count of trees growing in a southern English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Sevenoaks is a town in Kent, a county in south-east England; the definition is the brief locator 'in Kent'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sevenoaks is a commuter town found in that south-eastern English county.

clue.text: See 22
Student to have audience with the king

parts.note: L is a learner, from the British L-plate for learner drivers
to have an ear is to have a hearing or audience

explanation.surface: A student is granted an audience with the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Lear is Shakespeare's legendary British monarch in the tragedy King Lear.

clue.text: Old emperor sat around on the right

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A former ruler sat on the right-hand side.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the emperor of Russia before 1917.

clue.text: Spear I had found in the river

indicators.note: found in says one piece is located inside another

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in England
I had contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: Someone recalls finding a weapon in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trent is one of England's longest rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A trident is a three-pronged fishing spear, as carried by Neptune.

clue.text: Hopelessness of the French couple

parts.note: des is French for 'of the' with plural nouns
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: A French pair falls into gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is the complete loss of hope.

clue.text: Cleaner to put a man off

definitions.meaning: a washing agent such as soap powder
a cryptic reading: deter a gent, splitting the word into to discourage plus a gentleman

explanation.surface: A cleaning product is said to repel men.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: split the word as DETER (put off) and GENT (a man).
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a cleansing agent used for washing clothes and dishes.

clue.text: Sovereign found in the desk?

definitions.meaning: a measuring stick kept in a school desk

explanation.surface: A monarch's whereabouts are traced to a piece of office furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler is both a monarch and a straight measuring stick kept with pens and pencils.
